question: Under physiological conditions most of the leukocytes found in the blood are:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Neutrophils -> most abundant leukocytes in the blood -> under physiological conditions -> 90% CHAIN: Lymphocytes -> second most abundant leukocytes in the blood -> under physiological conditions -> 80% CHAIN: Monocytes -> third most abundant leukocytes in the blood -> under physiological conditions -> 70% CHAIN: Eosinophils -> least abundant leukocytes in the blood -> under physiological conditions -> 90%
enhanced_information: Under physiological conditions, the most abundant leukocytes found in the blood are neutrophils, comprising approximately 60-70% of total leukocytes. Lymphocytes are the second most abundant, accounting for around 20-25% of leukocytes. Monocytes are the third most abundant, making up about 3-8% of leukocytes. Eosinophils are the least abundant, representing only 1-4% of total leukocytes. Evidence paths confirm the interactions of neutrophils and lymphocytes with leukocytes.
analysis: Leukocytes are a type of white blood cell, and under physiological conditions, the most abundant type of leukocyte in the blood is neutrophils.
